ENEL 585 – Rectifiers

Topic 10

Dr. Philippe Gray

Department of Electrical & Software Engineering

Rectifiers: The Plan

  1. Diode rectifiers: the method of assumed states, current commutation, the single-phase and three-phase bridges
  2. Phase-controlled rectifiers: thyristors fired at \(\alpha\), inversion, commutation failure
  3. Power factor correction: the boost and totem-pole PFC, and back to the H-bridge

Rectifiers Overview

  • Definition: rectifiers transfer power from ac to dc
  • Role: the grid is ac, so a rectifier is the front end of most electronic systems
  • Some applications:
    • HVDC transmission
    • Power supplies for electronic devices
    • Motor drives and industrial converters

Part 1: Diode Rectifiers

Method of Assumed States

  • Assume a state for each diode, on or off, over one interval (e.g. \(v_g>0\))
  • Solve the circuit for:
    • \(i_D\) in each diode that is on
    • \(v_D\) across each diode that is off
  • Check: on needs \(i_D \ge 0\); off needs \(v_D \le 0\)
    • If a check fails, flip that diode’s state and re-solve
  • From here on, plot against \(\omega t\), not \(t\): a period is \(0\) to \(2\pi\) at any frequency

Half-Wave Rectifier, Resistive Load

Assume \(D_1\) on for \(v_g>0\), off for \(v_g<0\):

\(v_g>0\), \(D_1\) on: \(i_d = v_g/R > 0\) ✓

\(v_g<0\), \(D_1\) off: \(v_{D1} = v_g < 0\) ✓

Suppose instead the opposite:

\(v_g>0\), \(D_1\) off: \(v_{D1} = v_g > 0\) ✗

\(v_g<0\), \(D_1\) on: \(i_d = v_g/R < 0\) ✗

Half-Wave Rectifier, Average Output Voltage

\(0<\omega t<\pi\): \(D_1\) on, \(v_d = v_g\)

\(\pi<\omega t<2\pi\): \(D_1\) off, \(i_d = 0\), \(v_d = 0\)

Average output voltage:

\[\langle v_d\rangle=\frac{1}{2\pi}\Bigl[\int_0^{\pi}\hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta+\int_{\pi}^{2\pi}0\,d\theta\Bigr]\]

\[\phantom{\langle v_d\rangle}=\frac{\hat V_g}{2\pi}\bigl[-\cos\theta\bigr]_0^{\pi}=\frac{\hat V_g}{2\pi}\bigl(1-(-1)\bigr)\]

\[\phantom{\langle v_d\rangle}=\frac{\hat V_g}{\pi}\]

Half-Wave Rectifier with Freewheeling Diode

Assume \(D_1\) on for \(v_g>0\), \(D_2\) on for \(v_g<0\):

\(v_g>0\), \(D_1\) on: \(i_{D1}=I_d>0\), \(v_{D2}=-v_g<0\) ✓

\(v_g<0\), \(D_2\) on: \(i_{D2}=I_d>0\), \(v_{D1}=v_g<0\) ✓

Suppose instead:

\(v_g>0\), \(D_2\) on: \(v_{D1}=v_g>0\) ✗

\(v_g<0\), \(D_1\) on: \(v_{D2}=-v_g>0\) ✗

Concept of Current Commutation

Freewheeling diode \(D_2\); the load draws a constant \(I_d\)

\(0<\omega t<\pi\): \(D_1\) on, \(i_{D1}=I_d\), \(v_d=v_g\)

\(\pi<\omega t<2\pi\): \(D_2\) on, \(i_{D2}=I_d\), \(v_d=0\), \(v_{D1}=v_g<0\)

\(\omega t>2\pi\): \(v_g>0\) again, \(D_1\) on

Commutation

Current passing from one device to another

Here instantly: \(D_1\to D_2\) at \(\pi\), back at \(2\pi\)

Adding a Commutation Inductance

\(L_c\): source stray inductance, or an added inductor

Load unchanged: the constant current \(I_d\)

Effect

Commutation of \(I_d\) from \(D_1\) to \(D_2\) (and back) is no longer instantaneous: it takes an angle \(u\)

Four Intervals per Cycle with Finite Commutation Time

① Commutation (\(u\)): both on,
\(L_c\,di_g/dt = v_g\), \(i_g\) rises until \(i_{D2}=0\)

② \(i_{D2}=0\): \(D_2\) off, reverse biased by \(v_d = v_g > 0\)

③ Commutation (\(u\)): both on,
\(v_g<0\), \(i_g\) falls until \(i_{D1}=0\)

④ \(i_{D1}=0\): \(D_1\) off, reverse biased by \(v_g < 0\)

Finding the Commutation Angle u

x = 0.134 u = 30.0°

① both on: \(\displaystyle L_c\frac{di_g}{dt} = \hat V_g\sin\omega t\)

\(d\theta = \omega\,dt\): \(\;\omega L_c\,di_g = \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \omega L_c\int_0^{I_d}\!di_g = \int_0^u \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(X_c I_d = \hat V_g(1-\cos u)\)

\(u = \cos^{-1}(1-X_c I_d/\hat V_g)\)

More \(I_d\) or \(L_c\): longer overlap

Effect of Commutation on the Average

x = 0.134 ⟨vd⟩/V̂g = 0.297

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_u^\pi \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{\hat V_g}{2\pi}(1+\cos u)\)

where \(\cos u = 1-x\), \(\;x = X_cI_d/\hat V_g\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{\hat V_g}{\pi}\left(1-\frac{x}{2}\right)\)

\(v_d\) loses the area \(X_cI_d\) every cycle, the volt-seconds that ramp \(i_g\) to \(I_d\)

Single-Phase Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier

Assume \(D_1\), \(D_4\) on for \(v_g>0\), \(D_2\), \(D_3\) for \(v_g<0\):

\(v_g>0\): \(i_{D1}=i_{D4}=I_d\), \(v_{D2}=v_{D3}=-v_g<0\) ✓

\(v_g<0\): \(i_{D2}=i_{D3}=I_d\), \(v_{D1}=v_{D4}=v_g<0\) ✓

Suppose instead:

\(v_g>0\), \(D_2\), \(D_3\) on: \(v_{D1}=v_{D4}=v_g>0\) ✗

\(v_g<0\), \(D_1\), \(D_4\) on: \(v_{D2}=v_{D3}=-v_g>0\) ✗

Full-Wave Bridge Waveforms

\(0<\omega t<\pi\): \(D_1\), \(D_4\) on, \(i_g=I_d\), \(v_d=v_g\)

\(\pi<\omega t<2\pi\): \(D_2\), \(D_3\) on, \(i_g=-I_d\), \(v_d=-v_g\)

\(\omega t>2\pi\): \(v_g>0\) again, \(D_1\), \(D_4\) on

Commutation between the pairs: instant, at \(\pi\) and \(2\pi\)

vs half-wave: \(v_d\) repeats every \(\pi\), so its ripple is at \(2\omega\)

The Bridge With Commutation Inductance

\(L_c\): source stray inductance, or an added inductor

Load unchanged: the constant current \(I_d\)

Effect

Commutation of \(I_d\) between the pairs is no longer instantaneous: it takes an angle \(u\)

Current Commutation in the Bridge

① All four on, \(v_d=0\): \(L_c\,di_g/dt = v_g\), \(i_g\) rises to \(I_d\)

② \(i_{D2}=i_{D3}=0\): \(D_2\), \(D_3\) off; \(v_d = v_g\)

③ All four on, \(v_d=0\): \(v_g<0\), \(i_g\) falls to \(-I_d\)

④ \(i_{D1}=i_{D4}=0\): \(D_1\), \(D_4\) off; \(v_d = -v_g\)

Finding u for the Bridge

x = 0.067 u = 30.0°

① all four on: \(\displaystyle L_c\frac{di_g}{dt} = \hat V_g\sin\omega t\)

\(d\theta = \omega\,dt\): \(\;\omega L_c\,di_g = \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \omega L_c\int_{-I_d}^{I_d}\!di_g = \int_0^u \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(2X_c I_d = \hat V_g(1-\cos u)\)

\(u = \cos^{-1}(1-2X_c I_d/\hat V_g)\)

\(i_g\) swings \(2I_d\): a longer \(u\) than the half-wave

Average Output of the Bridge

x = 0.067 ⟨vd⟩/V̂g = 0.594

Steady state: \(\langle v_{L_d}\rangle=0\), so \(\langle v\rangle=\langle v_d\rangle\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_u^\pi \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{\hat V_g}{\pi}(1+\cos u)\)

where \(\cos u = 1-2x\), \(\;x = X_cI_d/\hat V_g\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}\left(1-x\right)\)

\(v_d\) loses the area \(2X_cI_d\) every half-cycle

Three-Phase Diode Bridge

Assume the top diode of the highest phase and the bottom diode of the lowest phase on:

\(v_{ga}\) highest, \(v_{gb}\) lowest, \(D_1\), \(D_5\) on: \(i_{D1}=i_{D5}=I_d\)

\(v_{D2}=v_{ba}<0\), \(v_{D3}=v_{ca}<0\) ✓

\(v_{D4}=v_{ba}<0\), \(v_{D6}=v_{bc}<0\) ✓

Three-Phase Diode Bridge: Any Other Pair?

Same interval, \(v_{ga}\) highest, \(v_{gb}\) lowest: suppose instead \(D_3\), \(D_5\) on

\(v_{D1}=v_{ac}>0\) ✗

Only the assumed pair passes (e.g. \(D_1\), \(D_5\) in the highlighted interval): top rail at \(v_{\max}\), bottom rail at \(v_{\min}\)

So \(v_d = v_{\max}-v_{\min}\): the largest line-to-line voltage, here \(v_{ab}\)

Three-Phase Bridge Waveforms

\(v_d\): six pulses per cycle, peak \(\sqrt3\hat V_g\)

Commutation: instant, every \(\pi/3\)

The Three-Phase Bridge With Commutation Inductance

\(L_c\) in each line: source stray inductance, or an added inductor

Load unchanged: the constant current \(I_d\)

Effect

Each of the six commutations per cycle is no longer instantaneous: it takes an angle \(u\)

Current Commutation in the Three-Phase Bridge

① \(v_{ga}>v_{gc}\): \(D_1\), \(D_3\) both on; \(v_d=\tfrac12(v_{cb}+v_{ab})\)*

② \(i_{gc}=0\): \(D_3\) off; \(D_1\), \(D_5\) on, \(v_d = v_{ab}\)

③ \(v_{gc}<v_{gb}\): \(D_5\), \(D_6\) both on; \(v_d=\tfrac12(v_{ab}+v_{ac})\)*

④ \(i_{gb}=0\): \(D_5\) off; \(D_1\), \(D_6\) on, \(v_d = v_{ac}\)

* derived on the next slide

Finding u for the Three-Phase Bridge

x = 0.050 u = 19.6°

① KVL: \(v_{ga}-v_{gc} = L_c\,di_{ga}/dt - L_c\,di_{gc}/dt\)

\(i_{ga}+i_{gc}=I_d\): \(\;di_{ga}/dt + di_{gc}/dt = dI_d/dt = 0\)

So \(v_{ga}-v_{gc} = 2L_c\,di_{ga}/dt\): \(\;v_{L_c} = \tfrac12(v_{ga}-v_{gc})\)

\(v_d = v_{ga}-v_{L_c}-v_{gb} = \tfrac12(v_{ab}+v_{cb})\)

\(v_{ga}-v_{gc} = v_{ac} = \sqrt3\hat V_g\sin\theta\), \(\;\theta=\omega t-\pi/6\)

\(d\theta=\omega\,dt\): \(\;2\omega L_c\,di_{ga} = \sqrt3\hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle 2\omega L_c\int_0^{I_d}\!di_{ga} = \int_0^u \sqrt3\hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(2X_c I_d = \sqrt3\hat V_g(1-\cos u)\)

\(u = \cos^{-1}\!\big(1-2X_c I_d/\sqrt3\hat V_g\big)\)

Average Output of the Three-Phase Bridge

x = 0.050 ⟨vd⟩/V̂g = 1.606

No \(L_c\): \(v_d = \sqrt3\hat V_g\cos\theta\), \(\theta\) from a pulse’s peak

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{3}{\pi}\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\!\sqrt3\hat V_g\cos\theta\,d\theta = \frac{3\sqrt3}{\pi}\hat V_g\)

Overlap: \(v_d\) lower by \(v_{L_c} = \tfrac12(v_{ga}-v_{gc})\)

Area lost: \(\displaystyle \int_0^u \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta = X_cI_d\)

Six per cycle: \(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{3\sqrt3}{\pi}\hat V_g - \frac{6}{2\pi}X_cI_d\)

\(x = X_cI_d/\hat V_g\): \(\;\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{3\sqrt3\hat V_g}{\pi}\big(1-x/\sqrt3\big)\)

Part 2: Phase-Controlled Rectifiers

Half-Wave Phase-Controlled Rectifier

\(S_1\) turns on when \(v_{S1}>0\) and gated; off at \(i_d=0\)

\(0<\omega t<\alpha\), assume off: \(v_{S1}=v_g>0\), not gated ✓

\(\alpha<\omega t<\pi\), assume on: \(i_d=v_g/R>0\) ✓

\(\pi<\omega t<2\pi\), assume off: \(v_{S1}=v_g<0\) ✓

Half-Wave: Average Output vs Firing Angle

α = 60° ⟨vd⟩ = 0.24 V̂g

\(v_d=v_g\) from \(\alpha\) to \(\pi\), zero otherwise

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\alpha}^{\pi} \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \phantom{\langle v_d\rangle} = \frac{\hat V_g}{2\pi}\bigl[-\cos\theta\bigr]_{\alpha}^{\pi}\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{\hat V_g}{2\pi}\bigl(1+\cos\alpha\bigr)\)

\(\alpha=0\): \(\hat V_g/\pi\), the diode rectifier; \(\alpha=\pi\): \(0\)

Thyristor Bridge

Assume \(S_1\), \(S_4\) on, \(S_2\), \(S_3\) off, from \(\alpha\) to \(\pi+\alpha\):

\(S_1\), \(S_4\) on: \(i_{S1}=i_{S4}=I_d>0\) throughout ✓

\(S_2\), \(S_3\) off, \(\alpha<\omega t<\pi\): \(v_{S2}=v_{S3}=-v_g<0\) ✓

After \(\pi\): \(v_{S2}=v_{S3}=-v_g>0\), forward biased

Diode: turns on. Thyristor: off until gated ✓

\(S_1\), \(S_4\) still on, so \(v_d=v_g<0\) from \(\pi\) to \(\pi+\alpha\)

Thyristor Bridge Waveforms

\(\alpha\) to \(\pi+\alpha\): \(S_1\), \(S_4\) on, \(i_g=I_d\), \(v_d=v_g\)

\(\pi+\alpha\) to \(2\pi+\alpha\): \(S_2\), \(S_3\) on, \(i_g=-I_d\), \(v_d=-v_g\)

After \(2\pi+\alpha\): \(S_1\), \(S_4\) fired again

Commutation: instant, when the next pair is fired

vs diodes: \(i_g\) is delayed by \(\alpha\); \(v_d\) dips below zero

Average Output vs Firing Angle

α = 45° ⟨vd⟩ = 0.45 V̂g

\(v_d=v_g\) from \(\alpha\) to \(\pi+\alpha\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{\alpha}^{\pi+\alpha} \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \phantom{\langle v_d\rangle} = \frac{\hat V_g}{\pi}\bigl[-\cos\theta\bigr]_{\alpha}^{\pi+\alpha}\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}\cos\alpha\)

\(\alpha>\pi/2\): \(\langle v_d\rangle<0\), with \(i_d\) still positive

Reversing the Power Flow

\(\langle v_{L_d}\rangle=0\;\Rightarrow\;\langle v_d\rangle=v_o=\dfrac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}\cos\alpha\) \(i_d>0\), so \(P=\langle v_d\rangle I_d\) takes the sign of \(v_o\)

\(\alpha<\pi/2\;\Rightarrow\;v_o>0\;\Rightarrow\;P>0\): rectifier

\(\alpha>\pi/2\;\Rightarrow\;v_o<0\;\Rightarrow\;P<0\): inverter, the dc source feeds the grid

What the Grid Sees

\(i_g\): a square wave, \(\pm I_d\), delayed by \(\alpha\)

Fundamental: \(\hat I_{g1}=\dfrac{4}{\pi}I_d\), lagging \(v_g\) by \(\alpha\)

\(P=\tfrac12\hat V_g\hat I_{g1}\cos\alpha=\dfrac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}I_d\cos\alpha=\langle v_d\rangle I_d\)

Absorbs \(Q=\tfrac12\hat V_g\hat I_{g1}\sin\alpha>0\) for \(0<\alpha<\pi\)

RMS: \(I_g=I_d\), \(\;I_{g1}=\hat I_{g1}/\sqrt2=\tfrac{2\sqrt2}{\pi}I_d\)

Power factor: \(k_p=\dfrac{P}{S}=\dfrac{I_{g1}}{I_g}\cos\alpha\approx0.9\cos\alpha\)

Phase Control With Commutation Inductance

① From \(\alpha\): all four on, \(v_d=0\), \(i_g\) rises to \(I_d\)

② At \(\alpha+u\), overlap over: \(i_{S2}=i_{S3}=0\), \(v_d=v_g\)

③ From \(\pi+\alpha\): all four on, \(v_d=0\), \(i_g\) falls to \(-I_d\)

④ At \(\pi+\alpha+u\): \(i_{S1}=i_{S4}=0\), \(v_d=-v_g\)

vs diodes: the overlap starts at \(\alpha\), not at \(0\)

Finding u With Firing Delay

α = 45° x = 0.140 u = 19.7° commutation fails: needs 2XcId

① all four on: \(\displaystyle L_c\frac{di_g}{dt} = \hat V_g\sin\omega t\)

\(\displaystyle \omega L_c\int_{-I_d}^{I_d}\!di_g = \int_{\alpha}^{\alpha+u} \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(2X_c I_d = \hat V_g\bigl(\cos\alpha-\cos(\alpha+u)\bigr)\)

\(\div\,\hat V_g\): \(\;2x = \cos\alpha-\cos(\alpha+u)\)

\(u = \cos^{-1}(\cos\alpha-2x)-\alpha\)

\(u\) is shortest near \(\alpha=\pi/2\): \(v_g\) at its peak

vs diodes: same area \(2X_cI_d\), from \(\alpha\)

Average Output With Firing Delay and Overlap

α = 45° x = 0.140 ⟨vd⟩ = 0.36 V̂g commutation fails: needs 2XcId

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{\alpha+u}^{\pi+\alpha} \hat V_g\sin\theta\,d\theta\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{\hat V_g}{\pi}\bigl(\cos(\alpha+u)+\cos\alpha\bigr)\)

last slide: \(\cos(\alpha+u) = \cos\alpha-2x\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle = \frac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}\cos\alpha-\frac{2X_cI_d}{\pi}\)

vs diodes: same drop \(2X_cI_d/\pi\), any \(\alpha\)

How Far Can the Firing Be Delayed?

Overlap must end before \(\pi\): \(\;\alpha+u<\pi\)

Extinction angle: \(\gamma=\pi-(\alpha+u)\)

Limit, \(\gamma=0\): \(\;\cos\alpha-2x=-1\)

\(\alpha_{\max}=\cos^{-1}(2x-1)\)

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle \ge -\frac{2\hat V_g}{\pi}(1-x)\)

In practice: \(\gamma\) covers the turn-off time

Commutation Failure

Still assuming \(i_d=I_d\), constant: a current source

\(\alpha_1=140^\circ<\alpha_{\max}\): commutation completes

\(\alpha_2=165^\circ>\alpha_{\max}\): \(i_g\) turns back before \(-I_d\)

\(S_1\), \(S_4\) stay on: \(v_d=v_g\) swings positive

Fired again at \(3\pi+\alpha_2\): fails the same way

In a real system \(i_d\) then rises: next slide

Causes: late firing, a dip in \(\hat V_g\), a rise in \(I_d\)

After a Commutation Failure

Real dc side, finite \(L_d\): \(\;L_d\,di_d/dt=v_d-v_o\)

Inverting: \(\langle v_d\rangle=v_o\), so \(i_d\) only ripples

Failure: \(L_d\,di_d/dt=v_g+|v_o|\), so \(i_d\) climbs

In practice: fire earlier, to commutate again;
the dc source lowers \(|v_o|\), to stop the rise

Three-Phase Thyristor Bridge

\(\alpha\) counts from where the diode would turn on

\(\displaystyle \langle v_d\rangle=\frac{3\sqrt3\hat V_g}{\pi}\cos\alpha\)\(\displaystyle\;-\;\frac{3X_cI_d}{\pi}\) with \(L_c\)

As before: inverts past \(\pi/2\); needs \(\alpha+u<\pi\)
HVDC: two in series (12-pulse) at each end

α = 30° ⟨vd⟩ = 1.43 V̂g

Part 3: Power Factor Correction

The Diode Bridge Draws a Square-Wave Current

  • The diode bridge draws a square wave, \(i_g=\pm I_d\)
  • RMS values: \(I_g=I_d\), and its fundamental (dashed) \(I_{g1}=\tfrac{2\sqrt2}{\pi}I_d=0.90\,I_d\)
  • Power factor, real over apparent power: \(k_p=\dfrac{P}{S}=\dfrac{V_gI_{g1}}{V_gI_g}=0.90\)
  • Total harmonic distortion: \(\text{THD}=\dfrac{\sqrt{I_g^2-I_{g1}^2}}{I_{g1}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-0.90^2}}{0.90}=48\%\)
  • The harmonics are 48% of the fundamental

Why Power Factor Correction

  • Square-wave harmonics: \(I_{gh}=I_{g1}/h\) for odd \(h\), so 33% at the 3rd and 20% at the 5th
  • Europe limits each device (IEC 61000-3-2, up to 16 A per phase): 2.30 A at the 3rd, 1.14 A at the 5th
  • A 2 kW bridge on 230 V: \(I_{g1}=8.7\) A, so \(I_{g3}=2.9\) A and \(I_{g5}=1.7\) A, both over the limit
  • Goal: a sinusoidal \(i_g\) in phase with \(v_g\), so \(\text{THD}=0\) and \(k_p=1\)

What Load Draws a Sinusoidal Current?

  • What could we connect on the dc side of the bridge to get a sinusoidal \(i_g\)?
  • A resistor: \(i_g=v_g/R\), in phase with \(v_g\), so \(k_p=1\) and \(\text{THD}=0\)
  • Issue: \(v_d=|v_g|\) swings from 0 to \(\hat V_g\) twice per line cycle, but a dc load needs a steady voltage

Add a Boost Converter

  • We need two things at once: a steady voltage on the load, and a resistor-like current from the bridge
  • Add a boost converter between the bridge and the load: \(C\) holds the output steady, and \(L\) is in series with the bridge, so its current can be shaped
  • Seen from the boost, the bridge is a source \(|v_g|\)

The Boost as a Resistor

  • Goal: the grid sees a resistor, \(i_g=v_g/R_e\)
  • After the bridge, that means \(i_L=|v_g|/R_e\): the same shape as \(|v_g|\)
  • \(Q_1\) on: \(v_L=|v_g|\), so \(i_L\) rises. \(Q_1\) off: \(v_L=|v_g|-V_d<0\), so \(i_L\) falls
  • So a controller can switch \(Q_1\) to hold \(i_L\) on that shape, provided \(V_d>\hat V_g\)
  • \(R_e\) is not a component and not the load \(R\): it is the ratio \(v_g/i_g\) the control enforces
  • The power \(P=\hat V_g^2/(2R_e)\) goes to the load

The Duty Ratio Must Follow the Line

  • \(|v_g|\) barely changes within one switching cycle (60 Hz against tens of kHz), so each cycle is nearly a steady state: \(\langle v_L\rangle_{T_s}\approx0\)
  • \(\langle v_L\rangle_{T_s}=d\,|v_g|+(1-d)\,(|v_g|-V_d)\approx0\)
  • \(d(t)\approx1-|v_g(t)|/V_d\): the boost relation of Topic 3, at each instant
  • \(d=1\) at the zero crossings and lowest at the line peak; \(d\ge0\) there needs \(V_d>\hat V_g\)
  • Example: \(\hat V_g=170\) V and \(V_d=400\) V, so \(d\) swings between 1 and 0.58

Idealised PFC Boost Waveforms

  • \(i_g\) follows \(v_g\) apart from a small switching ripple: \(k_p\approx1\) and a very low THD
  • Thin traces: the real \(i_g\) and \(i_L\), rippling about their averages (peak \(\hat I_g=\hat V_g/R_e\))
  • Input power \(p=v_gi_g=P\,(1-\cos2\omega t)\), load power steady: \(C\) absorbs the difference, so \(v_d\) ripples at \(2\omega\) (Topic 8)

Removing the Bridge: Totem-Pole PFC

  • Boost PFC: three devices in the current path (two bridge diodes, then \(Q_1\) or \(D_5\)); totem pole: two
  • Fast leg \(Q_1\), \(Q_2\): switches at the switching frequency
  • Slow leg \(D_1\), \(D_2\): changes over once per line half-cycle

Totem Pole: The Two Half-Cycles

A boost in each half-cycle; the other switch is the synchronous rectifier

\(v_g>0\), \(Q_2\) on: \(L\) charges through \(Q_2\), back through \(D_2\)

\(Q_2\) off: \(Q_1\) carries \(i_L\) to \(C\)

\(v_g<0\), \(Q_1\) on: \(L\) charges through \(Q_1\), back through \(D_1\)

\(Q_1\) off: \(Q_2\) carries \(i_L\) to \(C\)

Back to the Single-Phase Inverter

  • Replace \(D_1\), \(D_2\) with MOSFETs \(Q_3\), \(Q_4\): the H-bridge of Topic 7, with the line on its ac side
  • Cost: under Topic 7’s PWM all four switch at the switching frequency, so more switching loss
  • Gain: no diode fixes the sign of \(i_g\), so \(P\) flows either way, ac to dc or dc to ac
  • Gain: \(i_g\) can lead or lag \(v_g\): supply or absorb \(Q\) to support the grid
  • Unipolar PWM: ripple at twice the switching frequency, so a smaller \(L\)

Rectifiers: Summary

Controls \(i_g\) against \(v_g\) Power factor, THD Power flow
Diode bridge none: \(\langle v_d\rangle\) set by \(\hat V_g\), less \(X_cI_d\) drops poor: \(k_p\approx0.9\) ac to dc
Thyristor bridge firing angle \(\alpha\): \(\langle v_d\rangle\propto\cos\alpha\) poor: \(k_p\approx0.9\cos\alpha\), absorbs \(Q\) either way, by the sign of \(\langle v_d\rangle\)
Boost PFC \(d(t)\) shapes \(i_g\) near unity, low THD ac to dc
Totem-pole PFC (diode slow leg) \(d(t)\) shapes \(i_g\) near unity, low THD ac to dc
Active rectifier (H‑bridge) bridge voltage sets the amplitude and phase of \(i_g\) any, set by control; low THD either way
